overview: Ashuchi, in Jainism, refers to impurity or defilement, often associated with physical and mental states that hinder spiritual progress. It encompasses both external and internal aspects of impurity. Externally, it relates to the cleanliness of the body and environment, highlighting the Jain emphasis on hygiene and ritual purity. Internally, ashuchi pertains to impurities of the mind, such as passions and attachments, which obstruct the soul's journey towards liberation. The concept is deeply rooted in Jain ethical and ascetic practices, where maintaining purity is essential for reducing karma and advancing spiritually.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Impurity is due to the perception of impurity.
primary_sources.notes: This sutra discusses the perception of impurity as a mental construct that affects spiritual practice.

misconceptions.myth: Ashuchi only refers to physical uncleanliness.
misconceptions.reality: Ashuchi also includes mental impurities, such as negative thoughts and emotions, which are considered equally important in Jain practice.
